Bolted to that wall and climbing from the lower left toward the upper right runs a heavy welded steel service stair, a single folded stringer with seven treads and seven risers, the whole assembly graphite #14171C, its edge paint chipped down to mill scale, its bolt heads oxidised, a fine grey dust line settled on every tread nose and a smear of boot rubber on the lowest one. Each of the seven risers is faced with a brushed steel register plate held by two countersunk screws, and each plate is deep engraved and warm white paint filled with one single line name, from the bottom tread upward in this exact order: «БАЗОВАЯ СТАВКА», «ЭКСПЛУАТАЦИЯ», «КОММУНАЛЬНЫЕ», «ОТХОДЫ», «ПАРКОВКА», «НДС», «ИНДЕКСАЦИЯ». The riser plates read as one steel register of seven rows, one row per step, so the payment literally becomes a staircase; the topmost plate, the one reading «ИНДЕКСАЦИЯ», is the only one whose engraving is filled with amber #E8A400 instead of warm white, and a thin amber leader line runs from it out to the right and stops. Standing free on the concrete in the left third of the frame, entirely clear of the stair and clear of every other element, is the hero of the picture: the single stencilled numeral «7», sprayed directly onto the wall as genuine industrial stencil work in amber #E8A400 with real stencil bridges inside the strokes, overspray freckles at the edges, one dried run at the bottom of the stroke and pigment thinned where the wall was rubbed; its cap height is fifty two percent of the frame height, which makes it by a wide margin the largest object in the image. Fixed to the concrete in the upper left, above the giant numeral, is a bolted brushed steel headline plate carrying, deep engraved and warm white paint filled, the exact Russian string «Ставка за метр это 1 строка из 7.» set on two lines broken after the word «строка», its cap height eight percent of the frame height, wide tracking, no hyphenation, the terminal full stop present. Stencilled straight onto the concrete directly under that plate, at one third of the headline cap height, is the exact Russian string «Остальные приходят в первом счёте» on one single line. In the far background, deep in ink black falloff, an overhead travelling crane girder crosses the top of the frame and a closed sectional gate is barely legible, matching the attached photographs. All lettering in the frame is one single dense contemporary condensed grotesque with the feel of technical documentation rather than of an advertising poster, upright, never italic, never outlined, never scripted, generously tracked in the headline and tightly leaded in the small type, and every character is physically part of the scene, deep engraved into metal and paint filled, stencil sprayed onto concrete or crisply letterpress printed into paper, so that it lies in the plane of its own surface, obeys the perspective of that surface, holds the raking light along its machined bevels or its ink bite, casts its own micro shadow and collects the same dust as the material around it, and is never a flat sticker, never a floating digital overlay and never a soft glowing graphic.
